props.statement: The project decided to deprecate broker.id in Kafka 4.4 and remove it in Kafka 5.0.

props.statement: Under EOS, returning RESUME for production errors may poison the transaction, causing the task to restart and reprocess the same bad record repeatedly.

statement.value: Under EOS, returning RESUME for production errors may poison the transaction, causing the task to restart and reprocess the same bad record repeatedly.

n_05456b5df7682edecbe6b175861421e3.value: Under exactly-once semantics, a production error that triggers RESUME may poison the ongoing transaction. The task will restart from the last committed offset and reprocess the same input records. If the computation is deterministic, the same bad output record will be produced again, leading to a repeated cycle of failure → restart → failure.

props.title: EOS production errors may crash-loop

props.statement: For serialization errors, RESUME works cleanly under both ALOS and EOS because the error occurs synchronously before the record reaches the producer.

statement.value: For serialization errors, RESUME works cleanly under both ALOS and EOS because the error occurs synchronously before the record reaches the producer.

n_05456b5df7682edecbe6b175861421e3.value: For serialization errors, this limitation does not apply — the error occurs synchronously before the record reaches the producer, so no transaction is affected and RESUME works cleanly under both ALOS and EOS.

props.title: Serialization errors RESUME safely

props.statement: A bounded replay window (e.g., 5 seconds) is safer than silently skipping live data, as it ensures no data is permanently lost.
